exposure: low Socioeconomic Index for Areas (SEIFA) score
cohort: Term singleton babies born at the Mater Mother's Hospital in Brisbane, Australia from 2007 to 2013
finding: Maternal public insurance status, breech presentation, non-cephalic presentation, intramuscular narcotic use, and presence of meconium were significantly associated with low Apgar scores, while socioeconomic factors, maternal insurance status, parity, mode of delivery, and meconium presence were associated with moderate scores.
mod_finding: Emergency caesarean birth was significantly associated with a moderate Apgar score, while instrumental birth was not.
